implementation_notes: C# has first-class interfaces, so DIP/ISP/LSP are structural. Prefer constructor injection over property or field injection; use `internal` plus `InternalsVisibleTo` to keep abstractions public but implementations internal; default interface methods let an interface evolve without breaking existing implementors, which is the practical LSP escape hatch.
idiom_name: interface + constructor injection + default interface methods
pitfalls: Property injection hides dependencies from the constructor and defeats LSP-aware construction-time checks.
A public class with a public parameterless constructor plus a DI path creates two construction routes that drift.
Interface default members can hide missing implementations instead of forcing them.
